### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/client`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **53** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **7** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/api.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**34** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 22ce3d13fec94dab9df67edccd9cc71277a99a68`.

⛔ **14** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **7** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/api.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `resolveProtocol (28 routes)`, `responseSchema (6 routes)`, `resolveObjectMasker (4 routes)`
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `master_detail (literal, 39 pages)`
- **8** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **212** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 22ce3d13fec94dab9df67edccd9cc71277a99a68` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `77d476ece3e70162a56844f46030ef8cf301ef3f` — the merge of head `170b86ad19fb0e32fa0fc1462ece83ab32ed28d0` into base `22ce3d13fec94dab9df67edccd9cc71277a99a68`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 77d476ece3e70162a56844f46030ef8cf301ef3f && git checkout 77d476ece3e70162a56844f46030ef8cf301ef3f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 22ce3d13fec94dab9df67edccd9cc71277a99a68 170b86ad19fb0e32fa0fc1462ece83ab32ed28d0 && git checkout -B drift-repro 22ce3d13fec94dab9df67edccd9cc71277a99a68 && git merge --no-ff 170b86ad19fb0e32fa0fc1462ece83ab32ed28d0

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 22ce3d13fec94dab9df67edccd9cc71277a99a68
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 22ce3d13fec94dab9df67edccd9cc71277a99a68` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `1e7a1b104ea5f7afccee6cb52f21b1c5fc01c501`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/app-bundle.zod.ts (`AppMetadataBundleResponseSchema`, its header, the two exported types), packages/spec/src/api/index.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-app-bundle-routes.ts (whole: `appNavigationReach`, `inboundRelationObjects`, `bundleValidator`, `BundleMemberFault`, `registerMetaAppBundleRoute`), packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts (`metaItemAnswerSources`'s fifth argument, the `appBundleHost` registration), packages/rest/src/rest-route-ledger.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server-registrar-files.ts, packages/client/src/index.ts (`AppBundleCacheResponse`, `meta.getAppBundle`, the private `fetch`'s `admitNotModified` and `meta.getCached`'s one-line opt-in), scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs, the five test files, the five generated spec artifacts, content/docs/references/api (generated), the strictness-ledger count, .changeset/27627-app-metadata-bundle.md + packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts on `main` (`MetaItemAnswer`, `createMetaItemAnswer`, `META_UNDETERMINED_CACHE_CONTROL`), packages/metadata-core/src/object-schema-fls.ts (`normalizeIfNoneMatch`), packages/rest/src/meta-item-history-routes.ts (the literal third segments under `:type/:name`), scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs (the governed register), PR #28320's file list

Inputs: card #27627 (body and all fifteen comments: the epic filing, spec seat 3's PR 1 landing 6533483101, spec seat 1's two claims 6538102504 / 6538108232 and their corrections 6538175648 / 6538237411 / 6538251138 / 6539077865, ui seat 2's notes 6538126238 / 6539052883, the two dev reports 6539053683 (Target 4, PR #28320) and 6539061874 (this PR)), PR #28287 (body, the docs-drift comment, the file list of 26 files, the diff of 1636 lines against `main` read whole, the commits from merge-base 53749673), the 54 check-runs on this head (read 2026-10-31T05:10Z: all 54 runs completed, none failed, none cancelled, none in progress; success: Build & E2E UI, Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint & Repo Gates, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Live E2E UI, PR-body guards (claim · duplicate · Part-of · single-writer path), Plan Test Core shards, Spec property liveness, Test Core, Test Core (all 8), Test UI, Type Check UI, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · workspace, TypeScript Type Check, filter; skipped: 18.x upgrade harness (opt-in), Auto Label, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate (matrix shard/3), Dogfood Verify CLI, Lint UI, Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in), Schedule gate · skip when a green push run covers the commit, Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), Test UI (matrix shard/16), UI Published Artifacts), and the tree at this head and on `main` for the items the Scope line names. The head is mergeable and clean against today's `main` (merge-tree clean; none of the files `main` moved since the merge-base is in this diff). The diff touches no governed surface in the register, so no Tier H gate applies.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The route delivers Target 2 as the card and the claim state it** - right. `GET {metaPath}/app/:appId/bundle` registers through the per-item registrar inside the `/meta` umbrella, so the anonymous deny and the type admissions wrap it; the query set is closed and empty (`refuseUnknownQueryParams` first, pinned: a 400 before any read). The app is read first; `appNavigationReach` walks `navigation`, every area's `navigation` and `children` at any depth, collecting `objectName` / `viewName`, `pageName`, `dashboardName` once each in order; `inboundRelationObjects` adds one hop of `lookup` / `master_detail` referrers from the whole-type object list, from either stored shape of `fields`; views and pages bound to a served object join the navigation's by `deriveViewContainerObject` and `page.object`; dashboards are the navigation's. Every rule in the spec header has a pinned case.
- **One gate, no copy** - right, and this is the judgment that matters. Every member, the app included, is `createMetaItemAnswer` over `getMetaItem({ type, name })` under the rendered read's policy and the member type's own masker (resolved once per type per request), with `metaItemAnswerSources` handed the member's type. A `refuse` of any reason, or the bare not-found the item read serves as absent, leaves the member out; the app's `refuse` is sent by `sendMetaReadRefusal` and its absence by `sendMetaItemAbsent`, so an unknown or gated app answers exactly what `GET /meta/app/{appId}` answers (pinned byte for byte, status and body, and only the app read runs). A mask fault on any member is the whole answer (`sendFieldVisibilityFault`), never an absence. The byte-equality test runs every member of both callers' bundles against that caller's own item read.
- **The validator is per caller by construction** - right. The strong `ETag` is the SHA-256 of the JSON this response sends, after every gate, mask and translation, so it folds every dimension the item routes fold and the locale; `Cache-Control: private, no-cache` and `Vary: Accept-Language` are set; `If-None-Match` is compared through `normalizeIfNoneMatch`, which strips both the quotes and a `W/` prefix, and a match answers 304 with no body. When any served member carries the undetermined `cacheControl`, the bundle goes out `private, no-store` with no validator, which is the item read's own arm. Pinned: differing gates give differing tags, one caller twice gives one, another caller's tag or a changed store answers 200 with a new tag, the no-store arm; the ablation that hashed the keys alone went red on exactly the two per-caller cases.
- **No path shadows and nothing shadowed** - right. The literal `bundle` sits under `app/:appId`, three segments below `/meta`; every per-item sub-resource on `main` is `:type/:name` plus a literal (`history`, `audit`, `publish`, `rollback`, `diff`, `published`), and no route on `main` has a parameter third segment, so the new path matches only itself and the item read, the writes and the sub-resources keep their matches.
- **`metaItemAnswerSources`'s fifth argument** - right. It defaults to `req.params.type`, so the item routes are unchanged; only the bundle passes a type.
- **The client** - right. `meta.getAppBundle(appId, { ifNoneMatch })` follows `meta.getCached`'s spelling (`notModified`, `etag: { value, weak }`), encodes the id, and opts into the private `fetch`'s `admitNotModified` so a 304 is the answer and not a thrown failure; every other call keeps the throw (the flag defaults off). A refusal still rejects with the server's status and code (pinned). The head's last commit also passes the opt-in from `meta.getCached`, so its existing 304 branch, unreachable on `main` because the transport threw first, now runs and answers `{ notModified: true }` as its own docblock always said; pinned with two added cases (the 304 answer with the validator sent, and a refusal still rejecting), and named in the changeset.
- **Server-Timing** - the member reads run under `measureServerTiming('meta', …)`, so a `meta` span sits beside `db` and `total` under the existing gate; pinned once. Opening the header to every caller is Target 4's, not this PR's.
- **Ledgers, censuses and generated artifacts** - the route-ledger row (`sdk`, `meta.getAppBundle`, `AppMetadataBundleResponseSchema`, answered bare), both registrar lists, the mount-table pin rows, the canonical-query and docblock floors, and the `check-route-envelope` MODULES row (2 bare responses, 0 ok / 0 err, ratcheted on #9559 like `record-page-routes.ts`) are all present; the spec surface artifacts, the strictness-ledger count, `llms.txt` and the generated reference page follow. `Skills-docs: none edited` holds: no skill names an `api/` schema file.
- **Check-runs as gate verdicts** - read as above; every run on this head completed and none is red, cancelled or in progress at the read.

### ② Semver level

- **`@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/client` all minor; `Clause-②: yes (widening)`; `Metadata-protocol: added`** - accepted. A new route, a new exported response schema and a new client method, with no existing route, key or answer changed; `Metadata-protocol: added` is the right declaration for a new shape on the wire, and the lane's precedent for an added protocol shape is minor. The private `fetch`'s third parameter is not on the public surface.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Serial overlap with #28320 (Target 4, same seat) on one file** - both add a MODULES row to `scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs`; the rows sit in different places, so the merge should be clean, but whichever lands second merges `main` and re-runs `check:route-envelope`. The body also commits to moving this route onto #28320's shared body-hash validator (`@objectstack/types` `representation-validator.ts`) if that lands first; until then the two rules are the same rule written twice, which is a named follow-up, not a defect.
- **Name approval owed to the maintainer** - `AppMetadataBundleResponseSchema` and `meta.getAppBundle` are new public names on the spec and client surfaces; the route path is the card body's own (Target 2). The seat records the approval when it lands.
- **The runtime dispatcher's `/meta` twin does not serve the bundle** - the same posture as PR 1's record-page route; a deployment that serves metadata through the dispatcher alone gets no bundle. Named in the body; the console consumer (ui seat 2) must read it through the `RestServer` mount.
- **Dashboards come from the navigation only** - by design, as a dashboard has no object binding; the spec header says so.
- **`meta.getCached`'s 304 now reaches its caller** - on `main` a matching `If-None-Match` rejected with a thrown 304 before the method's own branch ran; with this head it answers `{ notModified: true }`. A consumer that relied on the throw was relying on a defect, and the method's docblock always promised the branch, so this rides the minor bump as a fix; the changeset names it.
- **The console half is bound to this shape** - ui seat 2 lands after this PR; nothing in this diff touches the console.

### ④ Design judgment

- **Nothing blocking, and no should-fix on the diff.** Tried: an app whose navigation names an object the caller may not read (the gate has already pruned the entry, so nothing is reached through it, pinned); an object reached only through a gated object (absent, pinned); a view bound to a served object but gated itself (absent, pinned); a member whose fetch throws something other than the bare not-found (the whole request fails through `handleRouteError`, never a silent absence); a list read that throws (the same); a runtime without Web Crypto (served with no validator rather than a weaker one); `If-None-Match` with a weak prefix (matches). Deriving the member set from the app the caller is served, and answering each member through the one item chain, is the right shape: the bundle can never say more than the item reads would.

**Verdict reasoning.** The route is the item reads composed, as the claim demanded: one gate, one mask, one translation, per member, pinned byte for byte against the single reads for two callers, and a refused app or an unjudgeable member is the whole answer. The validator is the served bytes, so it is per caller without a second fold. The route sits where it shadows nothing, the ledgers and censuses are filled, the client opts into 304 narrowly, and semver is minor with the protocol addition declared. The overlap with #28320 is one file and a named helper move.

Scope: packages/rest/src/meta-app-bundle-routes.ts (the send site: `undetermined`, `sendMetaRepresentation`, `metaRepresentationCaching`; `bundleValidator` and the `normalizeIfNoneMatch` import removed; the module header), packages/rest/src/meta-app-bundle-routes.test.ts (the validator pins), packages/rest/src/rest-server-docblock-position.test.ts (the floor 16 to 15), scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs (the row 0 / 0 / 0), packages/spec/src/api/app-bundle.zod.ts (the header's wording), content/docs/references/api/app-bundle.mdx (regenerated), .changeset/27627-app-metadata-bundle.md (wording, and the `meta.getCached` bullet) + the files of record 6539412174, unchanged by the delta

This is a delta review of record 6539412174: the PR-only diff at 1e7a1b10 and the PR-only diff at this head were compared line by line with index and hunk-position lines stripped (206 lines of interdiff), and the merge commit f49b4787 was read in combined form, which shows no hunk: the merge of `main` (#28320 among 23 commits) resolved nothing by hand. ### ① Derived judgments

- **The delta is the merge, one refactor and one regeneration; the members are unchanged** - right. `appNavigationReach`, `inboundRelationObjects`, `BundleMemberFault`, the member build through `metaItemAnswerSources`, the refusal paths and the schema are byte-identical in both PR-only diffs; the interdiff is the send site, the validator pins, the docblock floor, the route-envelope row, and the wording of the header, the reference page and the changeset.

- **`metadata.enableCache: false` is now honoured** - right, and new: the first head always sent a validator; this head sends none and no `Cache-Control`, answering a matching `If-None-Match` in full, as the item reads do. Pinned. A behaviour change on an unreleased route, in the direction of the deployment's own declared setting.
- **The counts and ledgers follow** - right. One module-level helper fewer, so the docblock floor is 15 and the sum 95; the route-envelope row is `responses: 0, ok: 0, err: 0` because the module builds no response body itself; `scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs` is the one file this PR and #28320 both touched, and the merge took both rows cleanly.

### ④ Design judgment

- The delta removes a second validator implementation in favour of the one the `/meta` family shares, keeps the one exception the family has (tier 2) by the family's own signal, and gains the deployment switch the family honours. Fewer lines, one rule, nothing lost. Nothing to add to record 6539412174's ④.

**Verdict reasoning.** The merge resolved nothing by hand; the refactor replaces the bundle's own validator with the shared helper #28320 landed, keeping the per-caller rule, the tier-2 exception and adding the cache switch, each pinned; members, schema and client are unchanged; the semver stands; every check on the head is green or skipped. ## 维护者速读

- **改了什么：** 新增 `GET /api/v1/meta/app/{appId}/bundle`，一次返回一个应用的元数据：应用本身、导航能到达的对象及其关联对象，以及它们的视图、页面和仪表盘。每一项都和单独读取那一项时的权限结果一致，读不到的不出现。返回带按调用者计算的 ETag 和 `private, no-cache`，内容没变时回 304。客户端新增 `meta.getAppBundle`，`meta.getCached` 遇到 304 不再报错。
